The country is broadly workable, at the lower end, with one of Europe's most restrictive legal-gender-recognition situations. Lithuania's Civil Code grants the right to medically change gender in principle, but no legal framework regulating the procedure has existed for 17 years — a deadlock the Constitutional Court refused to resolve in September 2025, perpetuating what an ECtHR body called a "distressing legal uncertainty."

records.name: Latvia
records.summary_text:
Latvia is broadly workable with no legal framework for gender recognition — trans people cannot legally change their gender marker, leaving those who have transitioned in a legal limbo.
